page.layout: One printed page, numbered at the top left. Main text in one column; a section mark (manicule-like symbol) stands in the left margin beside the first lines. Narrow fragments of another page are visible at the right edge (show-through/neighbouring page edge) and are not transcribed.

main_text.p: gias, ingenia hominum tam varia & omnigenum vitiorum feracia. Rempub. Platonicam vel Utopicam somniare f•s est. Praeclare nobiscum agi putandum est, si non haereamus in ultima (ut dici solet) face Romuli. Necesse est itaque in omni Rep. aliqua mala non prohiberi, sed tolerari; multa bona non praecipi sed cujusque arbitrio permitti; utriusque generis plurima legibus praeteriri, & in medio relinqui: ne ex unius mali succidendi intempestivo studio, succrescant fortasse alia mala plura aut majora.

IX. Dubium tertium, de intentione Legislatoris: An & quatenus requiratur ad effectum obligandi? Quod est quaerere, si princeps nullo justitiae aut publici boni intuitu, sed odio aut gratia privata, sed ambitione & mera dominandi libidine, sed avaritia aliave prava impotentis animi cupiditate ductus, legem tulerit subditis; an illi ad parendum legi obligentur in conscientia? Facilis responsio, obligari; si non fit aliud impedimentum: id est, si qui legem tulit habuerit legitimam potestatem, & Lex ipsa fit alias justa, pro more gentis legitime rogata & sufficienter promulgata. Dico igitur primo, ficut in artificialibus non est semper idem finis operis & operantis; ut in domo aedificanda, finis operis (id est domus) est, ut sit commoda domino habitatio; finis operantis (id est Architecti) est, ut ipse ex labore lucrum percipiat; ita in Republica fieri posse, ut Legislator intendat commodum proprium, & ipsa tamen Lex tendat in bonum commune.

X. Objicies fortasse, finem sive intentionem minus rectam semper vitiare opus: ergo & Legislatoris pravam intentionem vitiare legem, quod est ipsius opus. Ut huic objectioni occurratur, dico secundo, intentionem malam semper vitiare opus, prout opus dicit actionem operantis: non semper vitiare

page.notes: Marginal section mark at the left of the first lines is a printer's symbol, not transcribed. Right-hand edge fragments belong to the neighbouring page. The paragraph after X is cut at the page foot; the last line "vitiare" sits at the right and is included as printed. Faint bottom-of-page marks are stains. Some words in the text are partly blurred (e.g. "succidendi", "f•s", "tuleritsubditis") and may be misread; "f•s" is a damaged word, presumably "fomniare fas est", the scan being unclear on the word "fomniare" and "est" partly hidden by a stain. Not confirmed: "fe-" / "Sed" lines at the top are fragments and the preceding page's last words are cut off.
